response.rationale: R3 is uniquely supported by the combination of prior breast carcinoma, atypical cells within dermal vessels, and strong GATA3 positivity in those atypical cells. CD31 positivity is limited to endothelial cells lining the vessels, so R2 misattributes the vascular marker; R4 lacks lymphedema and extremity distribution.

rejected.why: The atypical cells are GATA3-positive, not CD31-positive; CD31 positivity is confined to endothelial cells lining dilated vessels, so angiosarcoma is not supported.
Stewart-Treves syndrome requires chronic lymphedema and typically involves an extremity; here the face is involved and the GATA3-positive atypical cells indicate metastatic breast carcinoma.
